original_value: Over the past two decades, automatic facial emotion recognition has received enormous attention. This is due to the increase in the need for behavioral biometric systems and human–machine interaction where the facial emotion recognition and the intensity of emotion play vital roles. The existing works usually do not encode the intensity of the observed facial emotion and even less involve modeling the multi-class facial behavior data jointly. Our work involves recognizing the emotion along with the respective intensities of those emotions. The algorithms used in this comparative study are Gabor filters, a Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) for feature extraction. For classification, we have used Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Nearest Neighbor Algorithm (kNN). This attains emotion recognition and intensity estimation of each recognized emotion. This is a comparative study of classifiers used for facial emotion recognition along with the intensity estimation of those emotions for databases. The results verified that the comparative study could be further used in real-time behavioral facial emotion and intensity of emotion recognition.

result.paraphrase: Over the last two decades, automatic facial emotion recognition has drawn substantial attention because of the growing demand for behavioral biometric systems and human–machine interaction, where recognizing facial emotion and its intensity is essential. Prior work typically fails to encode the intensity of observed facial emotion and even less often models multi-class facial behavior data jointly. In this study, we recognize emotions together with their corresponding intensities. The feature-extraction methods compared here are Gabor filters, Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), and Local Binary Pattern (LBP). For classification, we use Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Nearest Neighbor Algorithm (kNN). This enables emotion recognition and intensity estimation for each detected emotion. Overall, it is a comparative study of classifiers for facial emotion recognition and emotion-intensity estimation on databases, and the results confirm that it can be extended to real-time behavioral facial emotion and intensity recognition.
